title: BCG consultants using GPT-4 finish 12.2% more tasks 25.1% faster with higher quality in a preregistered experiment (jagged frontier study)
summary: In a preregistered experiment with 758 BCG consultants, GPT-4 users completed 12.2% more tasks 25.1% faster with higher quality, but erred more on a task beyond its reach.
account: Researchers from Harvard Business School, Wharton, Warwick Business School, MIT Sloan and the Boston Consulting Group Henderson Institute ran a preregistered experiment with 758 BCG consultants, about 7% of the firm's individual contributor-level consultants. After a baseline task, the consultants were randomly assigned to work without AI, with GPT-4, or with GPT-4 and an overview of prompt engineering; all used GPT-4 as available at the end of April 2023 through a company platform built on the OpenAI API. On 18 realistic consulting tasks that the authors judged within the reach of the model, the consultants using AI completed 12.2% more tasks, finished 25.1% more quickly and produced work that human graders rated more than 40% higher in quality. Consultants below the average baseline score improved by 43% and those above it by 17%. On a business problem chosen to lie outside the model's reach, consultants using AI were 19 percentage points less likely to reach the correct answer. Harvard Business School released the working paper on 22 September 2023, and Organization Science published the study in March 2026. The tasks were designed for the experiment. Three of the nine authors worked for BCG, another advises BCG, and Harvard Business School paid for part of the research.
